summary: Well-designed, preregistered paired controlled-fault study with thorough execution accounting and archived artifacts. Primary paired analysis is appropriate and reported transparently. The main preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (effect on verifier+simulator pass rate) is supported by the paired counts and exact test. However a preregistered confirmatory safety analysis (harmful over-repair threshold) is not reported in the manuscript/analysis outputs; the manuscript must either present that archived analysis or explicitly disclose it as unexecuted and state the implications. Minor reference and disclosure polishing is suggested but not blocking.
critical_issues: A preregistered confirmatory hypothesis about harmful over-repair (<=5% absolute increase) is listed in the preregistration but no confirmatory result or explicit disclosure that it was unexecuted appears in the manuscript or analysis outputs. This is a required preregistration-analysis fidelity issue that must be resolved in the paper (see Required Revisions).
required_revisions: Either (A) present the archived confirmatory harmful-overrepair analysis exactly as executed (counts, proportions, CI, and whether the <=5% threshold was met) using the existing archived artifacts, or (B) if that preregistered confirmatory analysis was not executed, explicitly state in Methods and Results that the harmful-overrepair confirmatory test was not performed, describe why (infrastructure, analysis executor choice, or other archival reason), and clarify how this omission affects interpretation and conclusions (i.e., remove or qualify any implicit safety claims tied to that preregistered hypothesis).
optional_revisions: Polish the Disclosure Statement to be more concise while preserving the mandatory master-prompt archive reference and required procedural disclosures (avoid repeating execution accounting already documented in the manifest).

If available in the archived artifacts, add a brief summarized table or paragraph reporting harmful-edit / intent-changing audit counts and a short descriptive per-fault-class breakdown in the Supplementary/archival artifacts and reference it from the manuscript (labelled exploratory).

Ensure each References entry contains full bibliographic metadata where available (authors, title, venue, year) even when DOI/arXiv is included; this is stylistic/formatting polish rather than a substantive defect.
